content: 1. Efavirenz and olanzapine both have the potential to prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be used with caution, and close monitoring is recommended. Limited data, including case reports, suggest that olanzapine may rarely cause significant QTc prolongation. 2. Efavirenz reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of olaparib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inducers cannot be avoided, monitor closely for reduced efficacy of olaparib. 3. Efavirenz decreases the levels and effects of oliceridine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is necessary, consider increasing the oliceridine dose until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. Both efavirenz and oliceridine increase sedation, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 4. Efavirenz and olodaterol (inhaled) both prolong the QTc interval. Use this combination cautiously and monitor closely. 5. Efavirenz and olopatadine (intranasal) both increase sedation, which can lead to additive impairment of psychomotor performance and daytime functioning. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 6. Efavirenz reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of olutasidenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers decrease olutasidenib concentrations and efficacy. Alternative drugs should be used. 7. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of omaveloxolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 8. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Efavirenz increases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, while also decreasing its levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of ondansetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 11. Efavirenz and opicapone both increase sedation. Use this combination cautiously and monitor closely. 12. Orlistat reduces the levels and effects of efavirenz by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if an increased viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 13. Efavirenz and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval. Efavirenz also reduces the levels and effects of osilodrostat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Adjust the osilodrostat dose if necessary. 14. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of osimertinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 15. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of ospemifene by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Oxaliplatin increases the levels and effects of efavirenz through an unspecified mechanism. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 17. Oxcarbazepine reduces the levels and effects of efavirenz by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of oxybutynin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of oxycodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Efavirenz and ozanimod both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 21. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of paclitaxel and paclitaxel protein-bound formulations by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 22. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of palbociclib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 23. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of palovarotene by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 24. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of panobinostat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating the use of alternative drugs. 25. Efavirenz increases the levels and effects of pantoprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Efavirenz increases the levels and effects of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism, while also reducing its levels via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of paricalcitol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Efavirenz and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Use this combination cautiously and monitor closely. 29. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of pazopanib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 30. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of pemigatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 31. Efavirenz and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 32. Pentobarbital reduces the levels and effects of efavirenz by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 33. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of perampanel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 34. Efavirenz and perphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use this combination cautiously and monitor closely. 35. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of pexidartinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, pexidartinib can cause hepatotoxicity. Avoid coadministration with other hepatotoxic agents. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 36. Phenobarbital reduces the levels and effects of efavirenz by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 37. Efavirenz increases the levels and effects of phenytoin by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism, while phenytoin reduces the levels and effects of efavirenz by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Periodic monitoring of efavirenz efficacy and phenytoin plasma concentrations is recommended. 38. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of pimavanserin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration if possible, and monitor for reduced pimavanserin efficacy. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating the use of alternative drugs. 39. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of pimozide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 40. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of pioglitazone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 41. Efavirenz increases the levels and effects of piroxicam by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of pirtobrutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, increase the pirtobrutinib dose as needed. Monitor closely. 43. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of pitolisant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating the use of alternative drugs. 44. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, as polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to metabolites that are CYP3A4 substrates. 45. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of pomalidomide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 46. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of ponatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 47. Efavirenz and ponesimod both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 48. Efavirenz and posaconazole both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. Posaconazole may also increase efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, but the clinical significance is unknown. 49. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of pralsetinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, double the pralsetinib dose starting on Day 7 of coadministration. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A inducer for at least 14 days. 50. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of praziquantel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 51. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of prednisolone and prednisone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of pretomanid by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents during pretomanid therapy. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 53. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of primaquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Primidone reduces the levels and effects of efavirenz by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 55. Efavirenz and procainamide both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 56. Efavirenz and prochlorperazine both decrease the QTc interval. Use this combination cautiously and monitor closely. 57. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of progesterone (intravaginal gel, micronized, and natural forms) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of proguanil by an unspecified mechanism, potentially decreasing the active metabolite's serum concentrations. Monitor closely. 59. Efavirenz and promethazine both decrease the QTc interval. Use this combination cautiously and monitor closely. 60. Efavirenz and propafenone both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 61. Efavirenz and protriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Use this combination cautiously and monitor closely. 62. Quazepam increases the levels and effects of efavirenz by inhibiting CYP2B6 metabolism, while efavirenz reduces quazepam levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely.
